audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never names one Locke ability. It reads 'his poke', 'his on-hit pattern', 'his escape' across all seven whys, both breakdowns and every spike.
audit.why: Riot gives him Silver Stake (P, on-hit magic damage that grows with the target's missing health), Ritual Nails (Q, 950-range projectile that marks, 10/9/8/7/6), Soul Ignition (W, 18/17/16/15/14, self-damage for attack and move speed, refunds part of the damage he takes at the end), Ashen Pursuit (E, a flat 10 seconds at every rank, 425 range, teleport-then-dash with an auto reset) and Purgatory (R, 120/100/80, 1000 range, execute). The full layer already carries these; the content layer was written blind.
audit.corrected: Named the real abilities through early, mid, late, all seven whys and the spikes, matching the facts the full layer already states so the two layers agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: Content spikes[2] hung Ambessa's first-item spike on Sundered Sky healing 'straight through his burst attempt'. That inverts the real item interaction in this matchup.
audit.why: Soul Ignition is what heals here: Riot's text says Locke takes damage during it and 'will heal back a portion of the damage he takes during the effect' at the end. Grievous Wounds cuts that refund. Ambessa lifesteal is not the spike — anti-heal is.
audit.corrected: spikes[2].text and whys[5] now put Grievous Wounds on Soul Ignition's 18-second window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Silver Stake's scaling was never stated, and the early breakdown told the player to 'chip him below half early' with no matching warning about their own health bar.
audit.why: Riot's text: his attacks 'deal additional magic damage On-Hit, increased based on enemy missing Health.' Every point of health you are missing makes his autos hit harder, and Purgatory then executes off the bottom of that. Sitting at 40% against Locke is worse than it looks.
audit.corrected: Stated in early and carried into late and the Purgatory floor line.

audit.whatIsWrong: Repudiation is absent from the whole content layer, and it is the cleanest answer Ambessa has to a mark cash-in.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Ambessa gains a shield, briefly braces herself, and then slams the ground... If she blocked any non-minion damage while bracing herself, this ability will deal increased damage.' Locke's kill script is blinking in and spending Ritual Nails marks on autos — dense, non-minion damage arriving in a predictable half-second. Bracing into it both eats the burst and pays for the slam.
audit.corrected: whys[3] now states the brace-into-his-cash-in play.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ashen Pursuit's auto reset is never flagged as a tell, and the content described level 2 as 'dash damage out-trades him' with no mention of what he actually does.
audit.why: Riot's text: he 'teleports to a location before dashing to attack his next target.' The kit derives an auto reset from it. The commit is the teleport, not the auto that follows — and because it is his only mobility on a flat 10 seconds at every rank, spending it forward is a one-way door.
audit.corrected: whys[1] and mid now name the flat 10 seconds and the one-way-door framing.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer Itemization row states 'Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal.'
audit.why: Grievous Wounds reduces healing, whatever its source. Soul Ignition heals him at the end of its duration, so anti-heal applies to it in full. The row talked a player out of the item that most directly answers his only sustain.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[0] is titled 'Punish the post-E window' but its body describes Ritual Nails marks and ends with a template tail, 'Only commit once it is down or baited', that fits neither.
audit.why: The title's subject is Ashen Pursuit. Its cooldown is the one flat number in the matchup — 10 seconds at every rank — and it is engage and escape in one button.

Two derived flags in Locke's kit contradict Riot's own text and I wrote around both. Soul Ignition is flagged trueDamage, but the true damage in Riot's description is what Locke deals to himself — it is not damage that bypasses your resistances, so the 'resistances-invalidated' entry in _missing-interactions.json misfires for this matchup. Purgatory is flagged grounding and zone; Riot's text says only that it damages and potentially executes enemies hit. I made neither claim.

notes: The full-layer entry for ambessa/locke is already strong and mostly correct — I reused its facts in the content layer rather than re-deriving them, so the two agree. Two things in the full layer I did not touch: it calls Locke 'a 125-range mana champ' in phases[0].why, breakdown.early and breakdown.wave, and nothing in the kit file gives his attack range, so I left the number alone rather than guess. Locke's kit flags Soul Ignition as trueDamage — Riot's text makes clear that true damage is self-inflicted, so the _missing-interactions 'resistances-invalidated' row for this matchup is a false positive; I did not write it. Purgatory's grounding and zone flags are also unsupported by its description.
